source: (The coffin laid upon two line-tubs, between the vice-bench and the open hatchway; the Carpenter caulking its seams; the string of twisted oakum slowly unwinding from a large roll of it placed in the bosom of his frock.—Ahab comes slowly from the cabin-gangway, and hears Pip following him.)
“Back, lad; I will be with ye again presently. He goes! Not this hand complies with my humor more genially than that boy.—Middle aisle of a church! What’s here?”
“Life-buoy, sir. Mr. Starbuck’s orders. Oh, look, sir! Beware the hatchway!”
“Thank ye, man. Thy coffin lies handy to the vault.”
“Sir? The hatchway? oh! So it does, sir, so it does.”
“Art not thou the leg-maker? Look, did not this stump come from thy shop?”
“I believe it did, sir; does the ferrule stand, sir?”
“Well enough. But art thou not also the undertaker?”
“Aye, sir; I patched up this thing here as a coffin for Queequeg; but they’ve set me now to turning it into something else.”

“Then tell me; art thou not an arrant, all-grasping, intermeddling, monopolising, heathenish old scamp, to be one day making legs, and the next day coffins to clap them in, and yet again life-buoys out of those same coffins? Thou art as unprincipled as the gods, and as much of a jack-of-all-trades.”
“But I do not mean anything, sir. I do as I do.”

“The gods again. Hark ye, dost thou not ever sing working about a coffin? The Titans, they say, hummed snatches when chipping out the craters for volcanoes; and the grave-digger in the play sings, spade in hand. Dost thou never?”

“Sing, sir? Do I sing? Oh, I’m indifferent enough, sir, for that; but the reason why the grave-digger made music must have been because there was none in his spade, sir. But the caulking mallet is full of it. Hark to it.”

“Aye, and that’s because the lid there’s a sounding-board; and what in all things makes the sounding-board is this—there’s naught beneath. And yet, a coffin with a body in it rings pretty much the same, Carpenter. Hast thou ever helped carry a bier, and heard the coffin knock against the churchyard gate, going in?
“Faith, sir, I’ve——”
“Faith? What’s that?”
“Why, faith, sir, it’s only a sort of exclamation-like—that’s all, sir.”
“Um, um; go on.”
“I was about to say, sir, that——”
“Art thou a silk-worm? Dost thou spin thy own shroud out of thyself? Look at thy bosom! Despatch! and get these traps out of sight.”

“He goes aft. That was sudden, now; but squalls come sudden in hot latitudes. I’ve heard that the Isle of Albemarle, one of the Gallipagos, is cut by the Equator right in the middle. Seems to me some sort of Equator cuts yon old man, too, right in his middle. He’s always under the Line—fiery hot, I tell ye! He’s looking this way—come, oakum; quick. Here we go again. This wooden mallet is the cork, and I’m the professor of musical glasses—tap, tap!”
(Ahab to himself.)

“There’s a sight! There’s a sound! The greyheaded woodpecker tapping the hollow tree! Blind and dumb might well be envied now. See! that thing rests on two line-tubs, full of tow-lines. A most malicious wag, that fellow. Rat-tat! So man’s seconds tick! Oh! how immaterial are all materials! What things real are there, but imponderable thoughts? Here now’s the very dreaded symbol of grim death, by a mere hap, made the expressive sign of the help and hope of most endangered life. A life-buoy of a coffin! Does it go further? Can it be that in some spiritual sense the coffin is, after all, but an immortality-preserver! I’ll think of that. But no. So far gone am I in the dark side of earth, that its other side, the theoretic bright one, seems but uncertain twilight to me. Will ye never have done, Carpenter, with that accursed sound? I go below; let me not see that thing here when I return again. Now, then, Pip, we’ll talk this over; I do suck most wondrous philosophies from thee! Some unknown conduits from the unknown worlds must empty into thee!”

modern_en.title: Chapter 127 — The Deck
paragraphs: The coffin lies on two line-tubs between the vise-bench and the open hatchway; the Carpenter is caulking its seams, the strand of twisted oakum slowly unwinding from a large roll of it tucked into the front of his smock. Ahab comes slowly from the cabin-gangway and hears Pip following him.
"Back, lad; I'll be with you again soon. He goes! This hand of mine does not do my bidding more kindly than that boy does. — Middle aisle of a church! What's here?"
"Life-buoy, sir. Mr. Starbuck's orders. Oh, look, sir! Beware the hatchway!"
"Thank you, man. Your coffin lies handy to the vault."
"Sir? The hatchway? Oh! So it does, sir, so it does."
"Aren't you the leg-maker? Look, didn't this stump come from your shop?"
"I believe it did, sir; does the ferrule stand, sir?"
"Well enough. But aren't you also the undertaker?"
"Aye, sir; I patched this thing together as a coffin for Queequeg, but now they've set me to turning it into something else."

"Then tell me: aren't you an arrant, all-grasping, intermeddling, monopolizing, heathenish old scamp, to be one day making legs, and the next day coffins to clap them in, and yet again life-buoys out of those same coffins? You are as unprincipled as the gods, and as much of a jack-of-all-trades."
"But I do not mean anything, sir. I do as I do."

"The gods again. Listen, don't you ever sing while working on a coffin? The Titans, they say, hummed snatches of song when chipping out the craters for volcanoes; and the grave-digger in the play sings, spade in hand. Don't you ever?"

"Sing, sir? Do I sing? Oh, I'm indifferent enough for that, sir; but the reason the grave-digger made music must have been that there was none in his spade, sir. The caulking mallet, though, is full of it. Listen to it."

"Aye, and that's because the lid there is a sounding-board; and what makes the sounding-board in all things is this — there's nothing beneath. And yet a coffin with a body in it rings pretty much the same, carpenter. Have you ever helped carry a bier, and heard the coffin knock against the churchyard gate, going in?"
"Faith, sir, I've —"
"Faith? What's that?"
"Why, faith, sir, it's only a sort of exclamation-like — that's all, sir."
"Um, um; go on."
"I was about to say, sir, that —"
"Are you a silk-worm? Do you spin your own shroud out of yourself? Look at your bosom! Be quick! and get these traps out of sight."

"He goes aft. That was sudden, now; but squalls come sudden in hot latitudes. I've heard that the Isle of Albemarle, one of the Galapagos, is cut by the Equator right in the middle. Seems to me some sort of Equator cuts that old man, too, right in his middle. He's always under the Line — fiery hot, I tell you! He's looking this way — come, oakum; quick. Here we go again. This wooden mallet is the cork, and I'm the professor of musical glasses — tap, tap!"
(Ahab to himself.)

"There's a sight! There's a sound! The gray-headed woodpecker tapping the hollow tree! The blind and the dumb might well be envied now. Look! That thing rests on two line-tubs full of tow-lines. A most malicious joker, that fellow. Rat-tat! So man's seconds tick! Oh, how immaterial all materials are! What real things are there, except weightless thoughts? Here now is the very dreaded symbol of grim death, turned by mere chance into the expressive sign of help and hope for life in the greatest danger. A life-buoy made of a coffin! Does it go further? Can it be that, in some spiritual sense, the coffin is after all only an immortality-preserver? I'll think about that. But no. I am so far gone into the dark side of the earth that its other side, the theoretical bright one, seems only an uncertain twilight to me. Will you never be done, Carpenter, with that cursed sound? I'm going below; don't let me see that thing here when I come back. Now then, Pip, we'll talk this over; I suck the most wondrous philosophies out of you! Some unknown channels from the unknown worlds must empty into you!"

modern_da.title: Kapitel 127 — Dækket
paragraphs: Ligkisten ligger på to linetønder mellem skruestikbænken og den åbne lugeåbning; tømreren kalfatrer dens sømme, mens tråden af snoet værk langsomt rulles af en stor rulle, der er stukket ind foran i hans kittel. Ahab kommer langsomt fra kahytsgangen og hører Pip følge efter sig.
»Tilbage, dreng; jeg er snart hos dig igen. Han går! Min egen hånd adlyder mig ikke mere villigt end den dreng. — Midtergang i en kirke! Hvad er her?«
»Redningsbøje, sir. Mr. Starbucks ordre. Åh, se, sir! Pas på lugeåbningen!«
»Tak, mand. Din ligkiste ligger belejligt ved hvælvingen.«
»Sir? Lugeåbningen? Åh! Det gør den, sir, det gør den.«
»Er du ikke benmageren? Hør, kom den stump ikke fra dit værksted?«
»Det tror jeg, sir; holder metalringen, sir?«
»Godt nok. Men er du ikke også bedemanden?«
»Jo, sir; jeg lappede den her sammen som en ligkiste til Queequeg, men nu har de sat mig til at lave den om til noget andet.«

»Så sig mig: er du ikke en gennemført, alt-grabbende, indblandende, monopoliserende, hedensk gammel slyngel, når du den ene dag laver ben og den næste dag ligkister at proppe dem i og endnu en gang redningsbøjer af de samme ligkister? Du er lige så principløs som guderne og lige så meget en altmuligmand.«
»Men jeg mener ikke noget, hr. Jeg gør, som jeg gør.«

»Guderne igen. Hør, synger du aldrig, når du arbejder på en ligkiste? Titanerne, siger man, nynnede stumper af sange, mens de huggede kraterne ud til vulkanerne; og graveren i stykket synger med spaden i hånden. Gør du aldrig det?«

»Synge, hr.? Om jeg synger? Åh, jeg er sløv nok til det, hr.; men grunden til, at graveren lavede musik, må have været, at der ingen var i hans spade, hr. Kalfatrehammeren er derimod fuld af den. Lyt til den.«

»Ja, og det er, fordi låget der er en klangbund; og det, der gør en klangbund i alle ting, er dette — at der ikke er noget under. Og alligevel klinger en kiste med et lig i stort set på samme måde, tømrer. Har du nogensinde hjulpet med at bære en ligbåre og hørt kisten støde mod kirkegårdslågen på vej ind?«
»Min tro, hr., jeg har —«
»Tro? Hvad er det for noget?«
»Jo, tro, hr., det er bare sådan et slags udråb — mere er det ikke, hr.«
»Hm, hm; fortsæt.«
»Jeg ville lige til at sige, hr., at —«
»Er du en silkeorm? Spinder du dit eget ligklæde ud af dig selv? Se på dit bryst! Hurtigt! Og få det skrammel af syne.«

»Han går agterud. Det kom brat, det der; men byger kommer brat i de varme egne. Jeg har hørt, at øen Albemarle, en af Galapagosøerne, bliver skåret af ækvator lige midt over. Mig forekommer det, at en slags ækvator også skærer den gamle mand midt over. Han er altid under linjen — brændende hed, siger jeg dig! Han ser herhen — kom, værk; hurtigt. Nu går det løs igen. Denne træhammer er proppen, og jeg er professoren i musikalske glas — dunk, dunk!«
(Ahab for sig selv.)

»Sikke et syn! Sikke en lyd! Den gråhårede spætte, der banker på det hule træ! De blinde og de stumme kunne man godt misunde nu. Se! Den ting hviler på to linetønder fulde af slæbetove. En yderst ondskabsfuld spøgefugl, den knægt. Rat-tat! Sådan tikker menneskets sekunder! Åh, hvor uvæsentlige alle materialer er! Hvilke virkelige ting findes der, andet end vægtløse tanker? Her har vi nu det frygtede symbol på den grumme død, der af ren tilfældighed er blevet til et sigende tegn på hjælp og håb om liv i den største fare. En redningsbøje lavet af en ligkiste! Går det videre? Kan det være, at kisten i en åndelig forstand trods alt kun er en udødeligheds-bevarer? Det vil jeg tænke over. Men nej. Jeg er så langt henne på jordens mørke side, at dens anden side, den teoretiske lyse, kun forekommer mig som et usikkert tusmørke. Bliver du aldrig færdig, tømrer, med den forbandede lyd? Jeg går under dæk; lad mig ikke se den ting her, når jeg kommer tilbage. Nå, Pip, nu taler vi det her igennem; jeg suger de mest vidunderlige filosofier ud af dig! Nogle ukendte kanaler fra de ukendte verdener må munde ud i dig!«
